seo.description: The HARAPPA mill — its looms, its process, and why Aizu Momen is nearly gone.

props.heading: Aizu Momen
body: The technique arrived in Fukushima in the Meiji era and stayed. Aizu Momen is woven densely, dyed in indigo, and finished so that it stiffens first and softens for years afterwards.
Two mills remain. That number is the entire argument for the work.
